# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 46–54/100, Unconfirmed → no, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 54. All results here are read from code. The score is low for two reasons. The site renders only in the browser, and the Trail guides page is marked "don't index". The one unknown is the canonical link (GEO-015). It stays unknown until you confirm your real domain. Band: **At risk** (taken from the low number, because confidence is High). ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Make pages render on the server (3 points lost) - **Why it matters:** many crawlers read only the HTML the server first sends and don't run JavaScript. With server rendering off, they may see an empty page. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Medium. Remove that line to turn server rendering on, or prerender the routes. - **Score after this:** 59–67 ### 2. Make the `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt an absolute URL (2 points lost) - **Why it matters:** crawlers expect a full address for the sitemap, so a relative path may not be followed. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4` - **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` - **Size:** Small. Change it to `https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml`, or whatever your real domain is. - **Score after this:** 54–63 ### 3. Link to Trail guides with a real link (2 points lost) - **Why it matters:** crawlers find pages by following `` links. A button that calls a script isn't one, so `/guides` is reachable only through script. - **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small. Replace it with `Trail guides`. - **Score after this:** 54–63 Not in the top three, but urgent: `/guides` is also blocked from indexing (GEO-014, 1.5 points lost). It is in your sitemap, so the signals conflict. - **Where:** `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` - **What the code says:** `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');` - **Fix:** remove the `/guides` rule. That alone takes the score to 47–55. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is plain text and valid | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have access | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` only disallows `/admin`. No config, so I assumed you want to be found. | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `server/middleware/headers.ts:3`. `/guides` is blocked and `/` is fine (1 of 2 routes clear). | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your domain | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical link in any file, and no domain declared in config | | GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `nuxt.config.ts:2` (both routes) | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4`. The sitemap is valid, but the `Sitemap:` line isn't absolute. | | GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Problem | Not run | `app.vue:2` and `nuxt.config.ts:6`. Every page gets the same title and description. `lang="en"` is set. | | GEO-016 | Server-rendered links to key routes | Problem | Not run | `pages/index.vue:8` (`/guides`) | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | Not run | `server/middleware/headers.ts` sets only `noindex`, not `nosnippet` | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Not run | Read `app.vue` and all three pages. No images, and the button has text. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. Never scored. | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app. Never scored. | ## Other problems found None found. ## Worth considering - **Say which routes exist:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `

Routes graded from easy to strenuous.

`. The page promises graded routes but lists none. Naming them, each with its own page and address, might give readers and machines something to quote. - **Home page says little:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `

Walks across the Peak District

`. The page has a heading and a button, and no text on what the walks are. A short intro might help. - **Per-page titles and descriptions:** `app.vue:2`: `useHead({ title: 'Trailhead' });`. Giving each page its own title, such as "Trail guides – Trailhead", would help people tell tabs and search results apart. - **Declare your site URL:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `https://trailhead.example/`. Setting the real origin in `nuxt.config.ts` would let canonical links be generated. - **Admin page:** `/admin` is both disallowed in `public/robots.txt:2` and marked `noindex`. That looks deliberate, so I left it alone. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015:** no canonical link exists, and no domain is declared except the placeholder `trailhead.example` in the sitemap. Tell me your real domain and I'll treat the rule as checkable. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **GEO-003:** the browser-only setting is explicit in config, so I counted it as a problem. A live scan would confirm what crawlers actually receive. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site, because there's no `geo.config.json`. - `trailhead.example` is a placeholder domain. - `/admin` is meant to stay private, so I left it out of the routes checked. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
